fixes.explanation: I see why you'd go there, but the text never ties these cities to where John the Baptist preached. It says they're the cities “…in which most of His miracles had been performed…” The miracles are the link, so keep your eyes on those.

Right on the money. Jesus says that if those miracles had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, “…they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.” Tyre and Sidon were cities outside Israel. Notice He says long ago.

That's the opposite of what Jesus says. He says Tyre and Sidon, cities outside Israel, “…would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.” Nobody gets driven away in that sentence. They would have repented.

That's it. Jesus asks Capernaum, “…will you be lifted up to heaven? No, you will be brought down to Hades!” It's a hard word, and the question He asks first makes the drop even bigger. I think this one stings.

Yes! Jesus says, “I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children.” Good news for a stamper with no diploma. The ones who receive it are little children.
